subsystems.role: seats the processor and feeds it a tightly regulated, high-current voltage.

subsystems.role: connect RAM and add-in cards at very high signalling rates.

buildSteps.title: Design the layout
buildSteps.detail: Engineers capture the circuit, choose a layer stack-up, and place every component. Thousands of traces are then routed with controlled impedance — differential pairs a few hundred micrometres wide must match in length so that signals arrive together.

buildSteps.title: Simulate before committing
buildSteps.detail: Signal-integrity and power-integrity software models whether fast buses such as PCIe and DDR will work, and whether the copper planes can deliver hundreds of amps without excessive voltage droop.

buildSteps.title: Generate the fabrication data
buildSteps.detail: The finished layout becomes artwork — one image per copper layer, plus drill files, solder-mask and silkscreen data.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the bare board
buildSteps.detail: Inner copper layers are patterned and etched, then stacked with insulating prepreg and laminated under heat and pressure. Holes are drilled, plated with copper to join layers, outer layers etched, and solder mask, silkscreen and a surface finish applied.

buildSteps.title: Solder the small components
buildSteps.detail: Solder paste is stencilled onto the pads; pick-and-place machines deposit up to a few thousand surface-mount parts per board; a reflow oven melts the paste in one pass.

buildSteps.title: Fit connectors and the socket
buildSteps.detail: Large through-hole and press-fit parts — CPU socket, DIMM and PCIe slots, rear I/O — are inserted and soldered or press-fitted, since they must survive repeated mechanical force.

buildSteps.title: Flash firmware and serialise
buildSteps.detail: UEFI firmware is written to the flash chip, and the board receives its serial number and hardware identifiers.

buildSteps.title: Test and inspect
buildSteps.detail: Automated optical inspection, X-ray of hidden solder joints under chips, in-circuit electrical tests, then a functional test with a real CPU, memory and graphics card.

buildSteps.title: Package
buildSteps.detail: The board is fitted with heatsinks, backplate and accessories, then boxed with documentation.

prerequisites.why: boards need 4–16 copper layers to route dense, high-speed wiring without interference.
components smaller than a grain of rice cannot be hand-soldered at production volume.
PCIe and DDR define the signalling that the traces must carry reliably.
the socket, wiring and firmware must match one specific processor family.

prerequisites.tech: Electronic design automation and simulation tools
prerequisites.why: no human can route or verify this complexity by hand.

pathway.milestone: mainstream boards with PCIe 5.0 and DDR5 support
pathway.unlocks: high-bandwidth storage, memory and graphics on a commodity platform.

pathway.milestone: PCIe 6.0 (64 GT/s per lane) and faster memory
pathway.unlocks: lower signal voltages and shorter trace lengths, pushing boards to more layers and better materials.

pathway.milestone: more power delivery and thermal management built into the board
pathway.unlocks: processors that draw hundreds of watts without separate add-in cards.
far higher bandwidth between chips, at the cost of a very different board architecture.
